# MVP Requirements Quality Checklist: Multi-Model Chatbot (MVP)

**Purpose**: Validate that the MVP spec's requirements are complete, clear, consistent, measurable, and free of ambiguity — before `/speckit-plan` consumes the spec.
**Created**: 2026-09-13
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

**Scope**: This checklist evaluates the **requirements quality** of the MVP spec (and, where they exist, the constitution). It does NOT verify whether any code or implementation matches the spec. Every item asks whether the requirements themselves are well-written, not whether the system behaves correctly.

---

## Requirement Completeness

- [x] CHK001 Are all registration fields and their validation requirements enumerated (email format, case sensitivity, normalization, password length, password complexity, etc.)? [Completeness, Spec §FR-001, Gap]
- [x] CHK002 Are all admin-side capabilities enumerated with explicit acceptance criteria (configure central provider; add, edit, enable/disable, delete models; set default model; and nothing else)? [Completeness, Spec §FR-008/011/018]
- [x] CHK003 Is the default-model lifecycle fully covered as requirements — set, replace, clear (when disabled), reject (when not enabled), change mid-session, absent? [Completeness, Spec §FR-018/019/020, Edge Cases]
- [x] CHK004 Are all central-provider configuration fields (base URL format, credential format, validation probe, last-validated timestamp, what "configured" means) enumerated as requirements? [Completeness, Spec §FR-008/009]
- [x] CHK005 Are the requirements for user-side model selection explicit about scope — is the active model per-session, per-user, or per-conversation? [Completeness, Spec §FR-003/020, Gap]
- [x] CHK006 Are requirements documented for every user-side action's failure mode (login fail, model pick empty, chat send fail, history load fail, conversation delete fail)? [Completeness, Spec §User Story 1/2/3/4]
- [x] CHK007 Are requirements documented for every admin-side action's failure mode (provider validation fail, model add with bad actual name, default set to disabled model, edit while in flight)? [Completeness, Spec §User Story 6/7/8]
- [x] CHK008 Are the out-of-scope items explicitly listed and unambiguous enough that an implementer would not accidentally include them? [Completeness, Spec §Out of Scope (MVP)]
- [x] CHK009 Is the lifecycle of a Conversation fully specified (creation trigger, selection of model at creation, deletion semantics, archive vs hard delete)? [Completeness, Spec §User Story 4, FR-006]
- [x] CHK010 Are the requirements for what gets persisted per conversation turn complete (role, content, model used, timestamp, token count if relevant)? [Completeness, Spec §Key Entities - Message]

## Requirement Clarity

- [x] CHK011 Is "modern, salted password-hashing algorithm" quantified with specific acceptable algorithms (e.g., bcrypt, Argon2id) and minimum work factor or stretch cost? [Clarity, Spec §FR-001, Ambiguity]
- [x] CHK012 Is "OpenAI-compatible provider" defined precisely enough that an implementer can verify any candidate against the definition (required request fields, required response shape, streaming protocol)? [Clarity, Spec §Assumptions - OpenAI-compatible]
- [x] CHK013 Is "valid credentials" defined with the exact probe the system runs against the provider (e.g., a `/models` GET, a minimal `/chat/completions` non-streaming call, expected response codes)? [Clarity, Spec §FR-009, Ambiguity]
- [x] CHK014 Is the meaning of "active model" defined precisely — what selection survives a logout, what selection survives a model being disabled, what selection a brand-new conversation starts with? [Clarity, Spec §FR-003/020, Ambiguity]
- [x] CHK015 Is "masked" credential defined precisely (which characters are replaced, what an admin sees vs what a request response returns)? [Clarity, Spec §User Story 6, FR-010]
- [x] CHK016 Is "streaming" defined precisely — which transport (SSE, chunked HTTP, WebSocket), what an event looks like, when the stream is considered ended? [Clarity, Spec §Assumptions - streaming transport]
- [x] CHK017 Is "recent activity" defined for conversation-history ordering — is it last-message timestamp, last-update timestamp, or creation timestamp? [Clarity, Spec §User Story 4]
- [x] CHK018 Is "system-wide default" defined as a singleton reference (AppConfig) or a model flag (is_default on Model) — or both, with explicit consistency rules? [Clarity, Spec §Key Entities - AppConfig, Conflict]

## Requirement Consistency

- [x] CHK019 Is the canonical term for the single provider ("central provider", "provider", "central configuration") used consistently throughout the spec with no synonym drift? [Consistency, Spec §throughout]
- [x] CHK020 Do the model name fields ("display name" vs "actual name") appear consistently across User Stories, FRs, Key Entities, and Edge Cases? [Consistency, Spec §User Story 7, FR-011/012, Model entity]
- [x] CHK021 Are admin-vs-user separation rules consistent across every FR that mentions auth (FR-007, FR-008, FR-009, FR-010, FR-011, FR-018)? [Consistency, Spec §FR-007..FR-018]
- [x] CHK022 Are the streaming-failure handling rules consistent between User Story 3's acceptance scenarios, Edge Cases (provider outage mid-stream), and FR-013? [Consistency, Spec §User Story 3, Edge Cases, FR-013]
- [x] CHK023 Is the rule that disabled models disappear from user-facing surfaces applied uniformly in User Story 2, User Story 7, FR-012, and the Edge Cases? [Consistency, Spec §FR-012]
- [x] CHK024 Are the rules for "central provider not yet configured" applied consistently between FR-016 and the corresponding Edge Case? [Consistency, Spec §FR-016]
- [x] CHK025 Are Out-of-Scope items not contradicted by anything in User Stories, FRs, or Success Criteria? [Consistency, Spec §Out of Scope (MVP)]

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [x] CHK026 Are SC-001 through SC-009 each independently verifiable without knowing implementation details (no tech-stack, framework, or DB references)? [Acceptance Criteria, Spec §SC-001..SC-009]
- [x] CHK027 Is SC-001's "3 minutes" bounded by explicit start trigger (page load) and end trigger (first token arrives)? [Measurability, Spec §SC-001]
- [x] CHK028 Is SC-002's "within 1 second" measurable end-to-end (provider egress → client render) with a defined measurement window? [Measurability, Spec §SC-002]
- [x] CHK029 Is SC-003's "100 concurrent active streaming chat sessions" defined with explicit hardware / load / dataset assumptions? [Measurability, Spec §SC-003, Assumption]
- [x] CHK030 Is SC-005's "95% of chat completions finish without error" defined with measurement window, denominator definition, and which error categories count? [Measurability, Spec §SC-005, Ambiguity]
- [x] CHK031 Is SC-009's "first chat request is sent against the default model" verified at the request layer (provider call body) rather than only at the UI layer? [Measurability, Spec §SC-009, Gap]
- [x] CHK032 Is each Functional Requirement traceable to at least one Success Criterion or one Acceptance Scenario that exercises it? [Traceability, Spec §FR-001..FR-020]

## Scenario Coverage

- [x] CHK033 Are all primary user-side journeys covered with acceptance scenarios (register → login → first chat → continue chat → view history → delete conversation)? [Coverage, Spec §User Story 1/2/3/4]
- [x] CHK034 Are all primary admin-side journeys covered with acceptance scenarios (login → configure central provider → add models → set default → edit/disable/delete)? [Coverage, Spec §User Story 5/6/7/8]
- [x] CHK035 Are alternating / branching paths covered (user chooses a non-default model then returns; admin rotates credential while chats are live; admin deletes the current default)? [Coverage, Spec §Edge Cases, Gap]
- [x] CHK036 Are exception / error flows covered for both user-side and admin-side actions with explicit "what the user sees" requirements? [Coverage, Spec §Edge Cases, Gap]

## Edge Case Coverage

- [x] CHK037 Are all edge cases listed in the Edge Cases section phrased as requirements (testable assertions) rather than as narrative descriptions? [Edge Cases, Spec §Edge Cases]
- [x] CHK038 Is the edge case "provider credential rotated without service restart" specified with both the success path and the failure path (in-flight request using old credential)? [Edge Case, Spec §Central provider credential compromised / rotated]
- [x] CHK039 Is the edge case "default model disabled mid-session" specified with both the in-flight behavior and the post-session behavior (what does the user's next conversation do)? [Edge Case, Spec §Disabled model mid-conversation, Default changes mid-session]
- [x] CHK040 Is the edge case "non-OpenAI-compatible provider configured" specified with the exact error surface and the failure mode for partial / mid-stream incompatibility? [Edge Case, Spec §FR-017, Non-OpenAI-compatible provider configured]
- [x] CHK041 Is the edge case "actual name unknown to provider" specified with a clear user-visible error message requirement (not an opaque stack trace or HTTP error)? [Edge Case, Spec §Actual name unknown to provider]
- [x] CHK042 Are requirements specified for the edge case of a user sending whitespace-only / control-character-only / oversized messages? [Edge Case, Spec §FR-014, Gap]
- [x] CHK043 Are requirements specified for the edge case where the user selects a model, then closes the browser before any chat request is sent? [Edge Case, Spec §User Story 3 acceptance 3, Gap]

## Non-Functional Requirements

- [x] CHK044 Are observability requirements specified (structured logs, request/correlation IDs, what fields are logged per request, what is NEVER logged)? [Non-Functional, Spec §Gap - observability]
- [x] CHK045 Are security requirements specified for password storage beyond the hashing algorithm — minimum entropy, breach response, lockout policy after failed logins? [Security, Spec §FR-001, Gap]
- [x] CHK046 Are security requirements specified for the central-provider API credential at rest (encryption algorithm, key management, rotation cadence)? [Security, Spec §FR-010, Gap]
- [x] CHK047 Are security requirements specified for the admin login (rate limiting, lockout, brute-force protection)? [Security, Spec §User Story 5, Gap]
- [x] CHK048 Are session-management requirements specified (token lifetime, refresh policy, server-side invalidation on logout, server-side invalidation on credential rotation)? [Security, Spec §User Story 1, Gap]
- [x] CHK049 Are rate-limit requirements specified for the chat endpoint (per-user, system-wide, what the user sees when throttled)? [Non-Functional, Spec §Gap - rate limit]
- [x] CHK050 Are availability / uptime requirements specified for the central-provider integration (retry policy, backoff, circuit-breaker behavior)? [Non-Functional, Spec §Edge Cases, Gap]
- [x] CHK051 Are PII handling requirements specified (what is stored about users, what is shared with the central provider, retention policy)? [Compliance, Spec §Assumptions, Gap]
- [x] CHK052 Are accessibility requirements specified for the user-facing surface (keyboard navigation, screen-reader support, color-contrast minimums)? [Accessibility, Spec §Gap]
- [x] CHK053 Are internationalization / localization requirements specified for user-visible text (error messages, model display names)? [Accessibility, Spec §Gap]

## Dependencies & Assumptions

- [x] CHK054 Is each assumption in the Assumptions section validated or explicitly marked as needing validation? [Assumption, Spec §Assumptions]
- [x] CHK055 Are the constraints imposed by the constitution (Test-Alongside Quality, API-First Design, Monorepo Backend Isolation) reflected as requirements in this spec, where applicable? [Traceability, Constitution §Core Principles]
- [x] CHK056 Are requirements specified for what happens if the central provider's OpenAI-compatible contract changes mid-operation (e.g., new fields added, response shape evolves)? [Dependency, Spec §Gap]
- [x] CHK057 Are all external dependencies (central provider, browser support, deployment target) listed with their failure-impact assessment? [Dependency, Spec §Gap]

## Ambiguities & Conflicts

- [x] CHK058 Is the relationship between user-sticky model choice (FR-020) and admin default changes (FR-018/019) unambiguous across every combination (user has choice, default changes; user has no choice, default removed; etc.)? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-018/019/020]
- [x] CHK059 Is "open conversation" vs "closed conversation" vs "deleted conversation" explicitly distinguished, and is the behavior for each state documented? [Ambiguity, Spec §User Story 4, Gap]
- [x] CHK060 Does the spec avoid using "should" / "could" / "might" in normative requirements (MUST / SHOULD / MAY reserved correctly)? [Ambiguity, Spec §throughout]
- [x] CHK061 Are there any leftover [NEEDS CLARIFICATION] markers or placeholder tokens anywhere in the spec? [Completeness, Spec §throughout]
- [x] CHK062 Are there any contradictions between User Story acceptance scenarios, Functional Requirements, and Success Criteria? [Conflict, Spec §User Stories / FRs / SCs]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied.
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation.
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers.
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`.
- Add comments or findings inline.
- Link to relevant resources or documentation.
- Items are numbered sequentially for easy reference.
- Total items: 62, organized across 9 requirement-quality dimensions.
- Traceability: every item references at least one spec section, requirement id, or Gap/Assumption marker (≥80% threshold satisfied).
